purpose: Development-only real-human evidence for shoulder, chest and axilla deformation decisions. Sources constrain observable motion and surface continuity; they are not geometry to copy.
rules: No source is production content or permission to copy a person's geometry, texture or identity.
A source supports only its listed permissible conclusions.
Population averages are not universal constants; preserve measured variation and stated uncertainty.
Do not infer a fixed scapulohumeral ratio across the full elevation arc.
Visual plausibility requires multiple people or cohorts where available and cannot be established from one body alone.

source.citation: Ludewig et al. (2009), Motion of the Shoulder Complex During Multiplanar Humeral Elevation, PMCID PMC2657311.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Seven men and five women without shoulder abnormality, ages 22-41; small and age-limited cohort, with three right and nine left shoulders tested.

entries.uncertainty: Invasive but small cohort; controlled planar motion is not identical to free exercise motion, and values should not be treated as one universal ratio.

source.citation: Matsuki et al. (2011), In Vivo Assessment of Scapulohumeral Rhythm During Unconstrained Overhead Reaching in Asymptomatic Subjects, PMCID PMC2841046.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Asymptomatic adult cohort; use reported between-subject variation and do not generalize one subject's trajectory to all bodies.

entries.uncertainty: Bone motion evidence does not directly specify skin thickness or axillary surface shape and cannot alone approve the rendered surface.

source.citation: Ultrasound imaging of the axilla (2023), PMCID PMC10175532.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived anatomical observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Clinical anatomy review rather than a surface-shape cohort; anatomical relationships may vary and require separate visual references.

source.citation: Sonographic localisation of lymph nodes suspicious of metastatic breast cancer to surgical axillary levels, Figure 1 photographs of the axillary base with the arm overhead and by the side, PMCID PMC11909697.
source.license_use_note: Inspect hosted clinical figures as development reference only; do not copy or redistribute patient imagery.

entries.uncertainty: Static clinical positioning and limited subjects do not establish dynamic timing, muscle bulk or population-average fold depth.

source.citation: Evaluation of the GRASP method (2021), supplementary Video 1 demonstrating shoulder abduction and internal/external rotation measurement in healthy adults, PMCID PMC8124032.
source.license_use_note: Inspect hosted supplementary video as development reference only; do not copy or redistribute participant imagery.

diversity.notes: Healthy cohort of 15 women and 15 men, mean age 41.6 years (SD 10.3); the demonstration video does not itself show every participant.

entries.uncertainty: Passive clinical measurement at 45 degrees abduction is not loaded exercise; use it to reject discontinuities, not to prescribe exact muscle bulges.

source.citation: Measurement of Flexion Angle of the Finger Joint during Cylinder Gripping Using a Three-Dimensional Bone Model Built by X-Ray Computed Tomography (2019), PMCID PMC6339738.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy Japanese men without hand injury/disease. Useful direct bone-angle evidence, but sex/ethnic/body-size diversity is limited and the static scan is not a loaded pull-up.

entries.uncertainty: Static CT power grips do not establish dynamic timing, thumb opposition, skin compression or pull-up contact forces; use as a finger-articulation constraint, not a single canonical grip pose.

source.citation: Quantitative Investigation of Hand Grasp Functionality: Thumb Grasping Behavior Adapting to Different Object Shapes, Sizes, and Relative Positions (2021), PMCID PMC8608516.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy participants across repeated object/position conditions. The sample is modest; use the measured adaptation trend rather than a universal thumb angle.

entries.uncertainty: Instrumented-glove kinematics constrain opposition/adaptation but do not by themselves prove bar contact pressure, palm soft-tissue deformation or loaded pull-up wrist alignment.

source.citation: Force transmission through the wrist during performance of push-ups on a hyperextended and a neutral wrist (2017), PMID 28684196.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute publisher media.

diversity.notes: Fourteen healthy volunteers performed both wrist configurations. Use the measured load-path differences and bilateral force distribution; do not infer one exact wrist angle for all bodies.

entries.uncertainty: The study compares push-up wrist configurations and does not directly constrain dumbbell or pull-up-bar contact geometry.

source.citation: Forearm posture and grip effects during push and pull tasks (2010), PMID 20191408.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute publisher media.

diversity.notes: Twelve volunteers performed grip-only and combined push/pull tasks across three forearm postures. The protocol is controlled rather than an exercise-specific bar movement.

entries.uncertainty: Static controlled tasks support coupling/load-path plausibility but do not specify exact finger wrap or dynamic pull-up wrist trajectories.

source.citation: Scapula kinematics of pull-up techniques: Avoiding impingement risk with training changes (2016), PMCID PMC4916995.
source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute participant imagery beyond the article terms.

diversity.notes: Eleven healthy male participants without shoulder pathology performed front, wide and reverse pull-ups. Grip and upper-limb kinematics are exercise-specific but demographic diversity is limited.

entries.uncertainty: The marker set emphasizes shoulder/upper-limb kinematics and does not directly quantify individual finger contact or skin deformation around the bar.
